#| label: meeting-attendance-setup
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false

resolve_meeting_dir <- function() {

  qmd_candidate <- tryCatch(
    knitr::current_input(dir = TRUE),
    error = function(e) NULL
  )

  if (!is.null(qmd_candidate) && length(qmd_candidate) == 1 && nzchar(qmd_candidate)) {
    return(dirname(normalizePath(qmd_candidate, winslash = "/", mustWork = TRUE)))
  }

  if (interactive() && requireNamespace("rstudioapi", quietly = TRUE)) {
    ctx <- tryCatch(rstudioapi::getSourceEditorContext(), error = function(e) NULL)
    if (!is.null(ctx) && nzchar(ctx$path)) {
      current <- normalizePath(ctx$path, winslash = "/", mustWork = TRUE)
      if (basename(current) == "index.qmd") return(dirname(current))
    }
  }

  stop("Could not resolve the Research Forum meeting directory.")
}

meeting_dir <- resolve_meeting_dir()

attendance_dir <- file.path(
  meeting_dir,
  "files",
  "meeting recap-attendance"
)

clean_path <- file.path(attendance_dir, "attendance_clean.csv")
summary_path <- file.path(attendance_dir, "attendance_summary.csv")

if (!file.exists(clean_path) || !file.exists(summary_path)) {
  source(
    file.path(meeting_dir, "scripts", "process_attendance.R"),
    local = TRUE
  )
}

people <- readr::read_csv(clean_path, show_col_types = FALSE)
headline <- readr::read_csv(summary_path, show_col_types = FALSE)

      '<span class="forum-pulse-label">Median time together</span>',

      <div class="forum-standout-card fade-in">

      <section class="forum-entry-section fade-in">

        <h2>The clinical question</h2>

        <p>
          Frontline immunotherapy can produce rapid and clinically meaningful
          responses in cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma. But once that response
          has occurred, an important question remains: <strong>how much additional
          treatment is necessary?</strong>
        </p>

        <p>
          The FIRST analysis examines whether early treatment response can help
          guide subsequent management, including the possibility of reducing
          treatment intensity rather than continuing therapy according to a
          fixed duration.
        </p>

      </section>

      <div class="forum-entry-takeaway fade-in">

        <span class="forum-entry-takeaway-label">Central Question</span>

        <p>
          Can the response already achieved after frontline immunotherapy help
          determine what treatment a patient actually needs next?
        </p>

      </div>

      <section class="forum-entry-section fade-in">

        <h2>Questions explored</h2>

        <div class="forum-entry-grid">

          <div class="forum-entry-mini-card">
            <h3>Early benefit</h3>
            <p>
              How much information about subsequent outcome is already present
              after the earliest doses of immunotherapy?
            </p>
          </div>

          <div class="forum-entry-mini-card">
            <h3>Dose intensity</h3>
            <p>
              Does additional treatment meaningfully improve outcomes once an
              early clinical benefit has been achieved?
            </p>
          </div>

          <div class="forum-entry-mini-card">
            <h3>Response-guided treatment</h3>
            <p>
              Can subsequent management be adapted to observed response rather
              than determined by a fixed treatment duration?
            </p>
          </div>

          <div class="forum-entry-mini-card">
            <h3>Treatment de-escalation</h3>
            <p>
              Could selected patients receive less systemic therapy without
              compromising meaningful clinical benefit?
            </p>
          </div>

        </div>

      </section>

      <section class="forum-entry-section fade-in">

        <h2>Why causal inference matters</h2>

        <p>
          Treatment intensity in FIRST was not randomly assigned. Patients who
          received fewer versus more doses therefore cannot be compared as if
          they had been randomized to those treatment strategies.
        </p>

        <p>
          The analysis used Bayesian causal methods to address measured
          differences between treatment groups and to estimate clinically
          interpretable relationships between dose intensity, early benefit,
          and subsequent outcomes.
        </p>

      </section>

      <div class="forum-entry-takeaway fade-in">

        <span class="forum-entry-takeaway-label">Methodological Principle</span>

        <p>
          The relevant question is not simply whether patients who received
          less treatment did well. It is whether the observed data support a
          credible estimate of what might have happened under different
          treatment intensities.
        </p>

      </div>

      <section class="forum-entry-section fade-in">

        <h2>Discussion themes</h2>

        <div class="forum-entry-topics">

          <ul>
            <li>Early response as a potential treatment-decision landmark.</li>

            <li>
              The relationship between cumulative dose intensity and subsequent
              clinical outcomes.
            </li>

            <li>
              <strong>Scheduled dose intensity versus delivered dose intensity.</strong>
              Ann W. Silk raised an important limitation in the original analysis:
              simply counting doses does not account for treatment delays or other
              deviations from the expected dosing schedule. That discussion prompted
              a regimen-adjusted dose-intensity sensitivity analysis that standardized
              observed treatment exposure to the expected interval for each therapeutic
              regimen.
            </li>

            <li>
              Confounding created by non-random treatment continuation and
              discontinuation.
            </li>

            <li>
              Bayesian approaches to estimating treatment effects in
              observational treatment patterns.
            </li>

            <li>
              The clinical rationale for response-adapted treatment
              de-escalation.
            </li>

            <li>
              How these findings might inform future prospective trials of
              individualized treatment duration.
            </li>
          </ul>

        </div>

      </section>

      <div class="forum-entry-takeaway fade-in">

        <span class="forum-entry-takeaway-label">The Broader Idea</span>

        <p>
          Instead of asking every patient to complete the same predetermined
          course of therapy, response-guided treatment asks whether subsequent
          management can reflect the benefit that an individual patient has
          already achieved.
        </p>

      </div>

      <section class="forum-entry-section fade-in">

        <h2>Toward response-guided care</h2>

        <p>
          The broader goal of FIRST is not simply shorter treatment. It is a
          more adaptive treatment strategy: initiate effective systemic
          therapy, measure early benefit, and allow subsequent management to
          respond to the biology and clinical response of the individual
          patient.
        </p>

      <section class="forum-entry-section fade-in">

        <h2>What happened next?</h2>

        <div class="forum-followup-card">

          <div class="forum-followup-eyebrow">From Research Forum to publication</div>

          <h3>The discussion changed the analysis</h3>

          <p>
            The March Research Forum was not simply a presentation of work in progress.
            Feedback from the group materially changed the manuscript. In particular,
            Ann W. Silk's observation that dose counts alone could miss treatment delays
            and other departures from the planned schedule led to the development of a
            regimen-adjusted dose-intensity variable for sensitivity analyses. The final
            paper explicitly acknowledges that contribution.
          </p>

      <section class="forum-entry-section fade-in">

        <h2>Who joined us?</h2>

        <p>
          The attendance record is preserved as part of the meeting recap. Teams participation signals are included only as a descriptive record and are not a measure of the quality of anyone's contribution.
        </p>

```{r}
#| label: attendance-table
#| echo: false
#| results: asis

roster <- people |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    Name,
    Minutes = round(duration_min),
    Camera = dplyr::if_else(any_camera, "●", "—"),
    Unmuted = dplyr::if_else(any_unmute, "●", "—"),
    `Raised hand` = dplyr::if_else(any_hand_raise, "●", "—")
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(desc(Minutes), Name)

cat(
  '<div class="forum-roster-summary">',
    '<strong>', nrow(roster), ' people represented</strong>',
    '<span>Sorted by time in meeting · ● = signal recorded at least once</span>',
  '</div>'
)

min_minutes <- min(roster$Minutes, na.rm = TRUE)
max_minutes <- max(roster$Minutes, na.rm = TRUE)

minute_fill <- function(x) {
  if (max_minutes == min_minutes) return("rgba(15,127,134,.16)")
  alpha <- 0.05 + 0.25 * ((x - min_minutes)/(max_minutes - min_minutes))
  sprintf("rgba(15,127,134,%.3f)", alpha)
}

html_escape <- function(x) {
  x <- gsub("&","&amp;",x,fixed=TRUE)
  x <- gsub("<","&lt;",x,fixed=TRUE)
  x <- gsub(">","&gt;",x,fixed=TRUE)
  x
}

cat('<div class="forum-attendance-scroll">')
cat('<table class="forum-attendance-table">')
cat(
  '<thead><tr>',
    '<th>Name</th>',
    '<th>Minutes</th>',
    '<th>Camera</th>',
    '<th>Unmuted</th>',
    '<th>Raised hand</th>',
  '</tr></thead><tbody>'
)

for (i in seq_len(nrow(roster))) {

  row <- roster[i, ]

  signal_cell <- function(value) {
    cls <- if (identical(value, "●")) " signal-on" else ""
    paste0('<td class="', cls, '">', value, '</td>')
  }

  cat(
    '<tr>',
      '<td class="name-cell">', html_escape(row$Name), '</td>',
      '<td class="minutes-cell" style="background:', minute_fill(row$Minutes), ';">',
        row$Minutes,
      '</td>',
      signal_cell(row$Camera),
      signal_cell(row$Unmuted),
      signal_cell(row$`Raised hand`),
    '</tr>'
  )
}

cat('</tbody></table></div>')

<script>
  document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", () => {

    const elements = document.querySelectorAll(".fade-in");

    if (!("IntersectionObserver" in window)) {
      elements.forEach(el => el.classList.add("visible"));
      return;
    }

    const observer = new IntersectionObserver(
      entries => {
        entries.forEach(entry => {

          if (entry.isIntersecting) {
            entry.target.classList.add("visible");
            observer.unobserve(entry.target);
          }

        });
      },
      { threshold: 0.12 }
    );

    elements.forEach(el => observer.observe(el));

  });
</script>
